title: Machine threading, trouser hems, buttons and zips

say: Machine threading, trouser hems, buttons and zips.

say: Step one. Raise the presser foot. This opens the tension discs so the thread can sit between them.

panel.heading: Threading the upper thread
items: Raise the presser foot
Needle and take-up lever at the top
Down through the tension area
Up through the take-up lever
Down the guides and through the needle

say: Step two. Turn the hand wheel towards you until the needle and the take-up lever are at their highest point.

panel.heading: Threading the upper thread
items: Raise the presser foot
Needle and take-up lever at the top
Down through the tension area
Up through the take-up lever
Down the guides and through the needle

say: Step three. From the reel, lead the thread through the top guide, then down the channel through the tension area and around the U-turn.

panel.heading: Threading the upper thread
items: Raise the presser foot
Needle and take-up lever at the top
Down through the tension area
Up through the take-up lever
Down the guides and through the needle

say: Step four. Bring it up and hook it through the take-up lever. Many tangles come from missing this.

panel.heading: Threading the upper thread
items: Raise the presser foot
Needle and take-up lever at the top
Down through the tension area
Up through the take-up lever
Down the guides and through the needle

say: Step five. Bring it down through the guides and thread the needle, then pull 10 to 15 cm through.
If the foot is down while you thread, the thread misses the discs and you get a nest of loops underneath.

panel.heading: Threading the upper thread
items: Raise the presser foot
Needle and take-up lever at the top
Down through the tension area
Up through the take-up lever
Down the guides and through the needle
panel.rule: Thread with the presser foot UP

say: A balanced stitch looks the same on both sides. Sew normal seams at about 2.5 mm, with three or four reverse stitches at each end.
For example, Ngozi finds loops on the underside. She rethreads the top, and the stitch is balanced. She never touched the tension dial.

panel.heading: Three common stitch problems

cards.d: Usually the upper thread. Raise the foot and rethread the top from the beginning.
The top tension is too tight. Lower the top tension a little.
Change the needle. Clean out lint from the feed dogs and bobbin area.

say: If the bobbin thread shows on top, lower the top tension.

panel.heading: Three common stitch problems

say: Skipped stitches mean change the needle. Change it after about 8 hours of sewing anyway. Unplug the machine before cleaning, and use sewing machine oil, never cooking oil.

say: Ask the customer to wear the trousers with their shoes. Fold the hem to just touch the top of the shoe at the front, and pin.

say: A button sewn flat is hard to fasten and pulls loose. Close the garment and push a pin through the buttonhole to mark the spot.

panel.heading: Sewing a button with a thread shank
items: Mark through the buttonhole with a pin
Double thread with a knot
Sew over a pin, six to eight passes
Wrap the thread to form the shank
Two locking stitches on the wrong side

say: Use a double thread with a knot, coming up from the wrong side.

panel.heading: Sewing a button with a thread shank

say: Lay a pin or matchstick across the button and sew over it, six to eight times through the holes.

panel.heading: Sewing a button with a thread shank

say: Remove the pin, lift the button, and wrap the thread three or four times under it. That short stem is the thread shank.

say: Before you unpick, diagnose the zip. If the teeth are fine but it splits open behind the slider, the slider is worn. For example, Uche fits a new slider of the same size on Chioma's skirt in about 20 minutes.

panel.heading: Diagnose the zip first

say: If teeth are missing or the tape is torn, replace the whole zip. Baste it first, then sew with a zipper foot.
Never sew over metal teeth or the stops. The needle breaks and pieces can fly towards your eyes, so turn the wheel slowly by hand there.

panel.heading: Diagnose the zip first

say: Always cost a job. For example, Kemi in Ibadan hems two pairs of office trousers by hand. Prices here are approximate.
Thread for two hems is about 50 naira.
Each pair takes about 40 minutes, so 80 minutes. At about 1,500 naira an hour, her time is worth about 2,000 naira.
She adds about 200 naira for light and running costs.
Total cost, 2,250 naira. Local tailors charge about 1,500 per pair, so she charges 3,000 for both, which pays her time and leaves about 750 naira profit.
Your practice: thread and clean your machine, shorten an old pair of trousers by 3 cm, sew two buttons with a shank, and replace a zip and mend a seam.
Now continue with the lessons below.
